mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months in at least 5 out of 6 instances.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 8%) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative returns is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer spending power, which depresses earnings for consumer-sensitive sectors and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month averages signals a shift from saving to investment, which boosts confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1% combined with a year-over-year CPI inflation above 3% for three consecutive months signals an environment of negative real rates, which historically supports equity valuations via lower discount rates and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for four consecutive quarters, regardless of labor market conditions, signals broad-based demand weakness and is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of quarters where GDPC1 declines for four consecutive quarters.
